summary:
EARTHBEAT is an interactive web application developed by MIVA COSMIX to make Earth science imagery more accessible through real-time sonification. Addressing NASA's Earth Information Jukebox challenge, it transforms visual information from NASA Earth visualisations into evolving musical experiences by analysing brightness, colour, intensity and movement across a 384-cell grid.

Its three-layer audio system translates standout visual elements into melody, dominant colours into harmony, and movement into pulse. Users can explore seven preset NASA visualisations or upload their own images and videos for sonification.

With interactive audio controls, frame descriptions and screen-reader support, EARTHBEAT provides an alternative way to explore scientific information, particularly for people with visual impairments.

By connecting science, sound and accessibility, EARTHBEAT makes Earth's changing systems more engaging and creates new possibilities for inclusive scientific exploration.
details:
EARTHBEAT: PROJECT INFORMATION

Team: MIVA COSMIX
Challenge: The Earth Information Jukebox

Project Overview

EARTHBEAT is an interactive web application that transforms Earth science imagery into sound, enabling users to experience scientific visualisations through both sight and hearing.

The application captures image or video frames and divides each frame into a grid of 384 cells. It analyses the brightness, colour and intensity of these cells while tracking visual changes and movement between frames.

Through real-time sonification, these visual characteristics are translated into musical elements using three independent audio layers:

- Melody: A playhead sweeps across the grid, translating standout visual cells into musical notes.
- Harmony: Dominant colours influence the harmonic characteristics of the sound.
- Pulse: Movement, changes and flashes influence rhythmic and pulse elements.

Together, these layers produce an evolving musical representation of the visual content. The sound is dynamically generated rather than prerecorded.

EARTHBEAT provides two modes of exploration:

- Preset Exploration: Users can select and explore seven available NASA Earth visualisations.
- Custom Exploration: Users can upload their own images and videos and experience their visual characteristics through sonification.

The application also provides interactive playback controls, individual audio-layer adjustments, exploration of visual areas, written frame descriptions and screen-reader support.

Benefits and Applications

EARTHBEAT offers several benefits across scientific exploration, education, accessibility and creative engagement.

Accessible Scientific Exploration: It provides an alternative sensory experience for people who are blind or have visual impairments, reducing dependence on visual interpretation alone.

Improved Science Communication: Complex visual patterns can be experienced through sound, creating another way to communicate scientific information.

Interactive Learning: Users actively explore sound, control playback and investigate different visual elements instead of passively observing charts or images.

Creative Engagement: By combining music, visualisation and science, EARTHBEAT makes Earth science more engaging for students, educators, researchers and the general public.

Flexible Exploration: Custom uploads allow users to explore visual content beyond the seven available preset visualisations.

Intended Impact

EARTHBEAT aims to make Earth science more inclusive, understandable and engaging by expanding how people access and interpret scientific information.

Its intended impact includes improving access to Earth science imagery for people with visual impairments, encouraging interest in environmental science and planetary systems, supporting alternative approaches to science education and public engagement, and demonstrating the potential of sonification as a tool for communicating complex visual information.

The project also seeks to inspire more inclusive approaches to scientific visualisation and data exploration.

Ultimately, EARTHBEAT seeks to change the relationship between people and scientific information by allowing them to experience patterns through more than one sensory pathway.

Tools and Resources

EARTHBEAT was developed as a browser-based interactive web application, bringing together modern web development technologies, visual processing and audio generation.

Development Technologies

- React.js: Used to build the interactive, component-based user interface and manage application functionality.
- TypeScript: Used to structure the application code, define data types and improve development reliability.
- Tailwind CSS: Used to create the application's styling, responsive layouts and visual design.

Development and Supporting Tools

- Visual Studio Code (VS Code): Used as the primary code editor and development environment.
- GitHub: Used for source-code management, version control and collaboration.
- Netlify: Used to deploy and host the application, making EARTHBEAT accessible through a public web link.

Scientific Data and Resources

- NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS): Provided Earth science visualisations and scientific imagery used for the preset exploration experiences.

Core Technical Processes

- Visual Processing and Analysis: Used to capture frames, divide them into a 384-cell grid and analyse brightness, colour, intensity and movement.
- Audio Generation and Sonification: Used to translate visual characteristics into the Melody, Harmony and Pulse layers.
- Image and Video Processing: Supports the exploration of uploaded images and videos.
- Interactive Web Technologies: Connect visual input, processing, audio generation and user interaction within the browser.

These technologies and resources work together to create an interactive experience that connects scientific imagery with sound.

Creativity and Innovation

EARTHBEAT approaches Earth science from an unconventional perspective: instead of limiting scientific exploration to what people can see, it allows them to hear visual information.

Its creativity lies in combining scientific visualisation with musical expression through a structured, three-layer sonification system.

The separation of Melody, Harmony and Pulse gives different visual characteristics distinct auditory identities. This allows users to experience multiple dimensions of visual information through one evolving soundtrack.

Another creative element is its dual exploration approach. Users are not restricted to predefined NASA visualisations; they can introduce their own images and videos and explore them through sound.

EARTHBEAT also combines technology with accessibility and creative storytelling, transforming scientific exploration into an interactive sensory experience.

It does not simply add music to science. It explores how sound itself can become a medium for communicating information.

Factors Considered

Accessibility and Inclusion: Accessibility was a central consideration in the development of EARTHBEAT. We incorporated screen-reader support, written descriptions of visual frames and audio-based exploration to make the experience more approachable for people with visual impairments.

Energy Efficiency: We prioritised a web-based experience that does not require specialised physical equipment. The application uses digital image and audio processing rather than dedicated hardware. However, formal energy-consumption benchmarking has not been conducted.

Cost and Affordability: We designed EARTHBEAT to be accessible through a web browser, reducing the need for specialised devices or additional equipment. The use of NASA's publicly available Earth science resources also supports accessible scientific exploration.

Usability and User Control: We considered the importance of allowing users to control playback, adjust individual audio layers and explore visual content at their own pace. This makes the experience more adaptable to different users and learning preferences.

Scientific Responsibility: We considered the distinction between representing visual characteristics through sound and extracting scientifically validated measurements. EARTHBEAT's sonification communicates patterns in visual content; it does not automatically establish the scientific accuracy of measurements extracted from every uploaded image.

Flexibility and Adaptability: By supporting both preset NASA visualisations and custom image and video uploads, we designed EARTHBEAT to accommodate different forms of visual exploration rather than restricting users to a fixed collection of content.

Conclusion

EARTHBEAT represents an intersection of science, technology, music and accessibility. By transforming visual information into an interactive auditory experience, MIVA COSMIX is exploring new ways to make our planet's story accessible to more people.

We believe that understanding Earth should not be limited by how much we can see.
